Thanks — reviewed the draft. A few technical clarifications we should bake into the final answers (keeps SecuredBank's three priorities covered):

1) Chokepoint / egress gateway: Our default hosted topology routes all outbound telemetry and third-party API calls through a hardened egress gateway (mutual TLS + strict allowlist). This is the only component with outbound Internet egress in the tenant path. The diagram labels this as "egress-gw-01" and the control plane enforces routing policies by customer tag.

2) Sidecar failure modes: Sidecars implement a local fail-closed policy — if the sidecar process or proxy healthcheck fails, the request is rejected locally; long-lived KV caches are tombstoned and not exported. For Dedicated/Private modes, we run an optional local-bastion proxy; if that proxy fails we fall back to an internal-swift path that is strictly intra-VPC and blocks outbound DNS/HTTP until operator remediation. I'll add the exact healthcheck signal and circuit-breaker thresholds to the doc.

3) Tenant separation & audit: Per-tenant metadata is stored with every inference request; we persist immutable telemetry (token counts, route, model-variant, VM/node id) to an append-only audit stream (retention configurable) and surface per-tenant views in Console. Access to raw audit streams is gated via RBAC and KMS-wrapped keys.

4) Evidence pointers: I attached a redacted network diagram (redwood_chokepoint_diagram.png). For compliance packet we can provide sample audit CSVs and a sanitized CloudWatch/Stackdriver trace export — need to confirm NDA scope.

Irene — can you confirm the wording around KMS and retention? Priyom — pricing/legal may want a short note on how evidence is shared (SFTP vs secure Drive).

- Ben
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
